evidence_quotes.quote: On estime à 90000 le nombre de ménages dans le comté qui utilisent des solutions alternatives aux réseaux municipaux (les solutions C et D). À Norrtälje, par exemple, dans l’extrême nord du comté, 44% de la population ne sont connectées ni au réseau d’eau potable, ni au réseau d’assainissement.

En matière de gestion, les services d’eau et d’assainissement sont sous la responsabilité des municipalités (soit seules, soit regroupées en organisations intercommunales), un fait rappelé par la loi suédoise sur l’eau entrée en vigueur en janvier 2007 (4).

Ce dernier autorise, sous certaines conditions, une tarification différenciée au sein des municipalités, fondée sur la variation des coûts de l’offre de services entre zones denses et zones peu denses.

La plupart des acteurs que nous avons interrogés s’accordaient pour dire que, de manière générale, le facteur clé expliquant ces différences est la densité non de la population mais du réseau (mesuré par la longueur du réseau/usager connecté).
“We encourage them to be permanent. But for that we have to supply them with water. Because they can’t live there because there are many of them that currently only have ‘summer water’” (11).

criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and community drinking-water and wastewater/sanitation service access across Stockholm County and specifically in Norrtälje municipality, comparing central municipal network connections, co-ownership mini-networks, and autonomous individual systems (wells and septic tanks), including summerhouses with seasonal 'summer water' converting into permanent residences.
criterion_notes.c2: Both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2 are satisfied (plain=yes, narrow=yes). Under the plain wording, the study analyses local and regional water/wastewater governance, land-use planning, and Sweden's 2007 Water Law. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it directly analyses multiple rule-type mechanisms governing service access and affordability: (1) tariff and cost-recovery rules (statutory full-cost recovery 'principe du prix coûtant', municipal tariff equalization 'péréquation municipale' across dense apartments and dispersed houses, the 2007 statutory rule permitting differentiated intramunicipal tariffs by cost/density, deficit rules permitting tax financing, and connection fee schedules); (2) permitting, enforcement, and discretion rules (official municipal environmental/health authorization and registration fees for off-grid installations, mandatory sanitation upgrades triggered by building-permit applications to convert summerhouses into permanent homes, coastal building dispensations, and extra building rights as incentives); and (3) ownership and collective-decision rules (unanimity rules for co-ownership mini-networks, statutory municipal obligation to connect properties when environmental hazards exist and a co-owner refuses, intermunicipal utilities, and Norrtälje's Veolia operational concession).
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical qualitative/mixed-methods case study drawing on semi-structured interviews with regional planning officials (RTK), utility leadership (Käppalaförbundet), and Norrtälje municipal officials and politicians (water/wastewater department head, former mayor), municipal policy/investment plans, and descriptive utility statistics from Svenskt Vatten (VASS) for 2007 and 2009. Qualitative socio-legal empirical studies are eligible regardless of lack of pooled quantitative effect estimates.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports outcomes directly relevant to connection, service availability, and affordability/tariffs: municipal water and sewerage connection rates across Stockholm County municipalities (Table 2, e.g. 56.07% in Norrtälje; ~90,000 off-network households county-wide), seasonal ('summer water' May–October) vs year-round water availability, household connection charges (~70,000 SEK vs ~150,000 SEK per house, Table 4), and annual household tariffs for apartments and single-family houses (Table 1) plus volumetric charges (Table 3).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (26 municipalities in Stockholm County, focusing on Norrtälje municipality's 55,530 permanent residents, 25,000–30,000 secondary residences, co-ownership associations, and apartment/households), legal/regulatory/tariff exposures, connection and tariff outcomes, and qualitative/mixed-methods empirical case-study design are clearly identified.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in French (with English interview excerpts). Although French is not among the three languages eligible without translation (Criterion 9), translation and full methodological/substantive assessment directly from the provided French full text is completely feasible per Criterion 10 and the study provides substantive socio-legal mechanism evidence; translation method/translator should be logged in extraction_note during data extraction.

study_design: Qualitative/mixed-methods empirical case study (semi-structured stakeholder interviews, municipal planning/policy document analysis, and descriptive utility statistics from Svenskt Vatten VASS)
population_and_sample: 26 municipalities in Stockholm County, Sweden (~2 million inhabitants, including ~100,000 summerhouses and ~90,000 households using off-network water/sanitation solutions), with an in-depth case study of Norrtälje municipality (55,530 permanent residents and 25,000–30,000 secondary residences). Units of analysis: municipality, residential zone/co-ownership, and household/property.
exposure: Swedish Water Law (2007) and municipal regulatory, permitting, ownership, and tariff/cost-recovery rules governing water and wastewater provision (full-cost recovery principle, municipal tariff equalization vs differentiated tariffs, unanimity rules and building-rights incentives for co-ownership mini-networks, mandatory sanitation upgrades upon building-permit conversion of summerhouses to permanent residences, environmental enforcement obligations, and private operational concession).
outcome: Household connection rates to municipal water and sewerage networks vs co-ownership mini-networks and individual off-grid systems, seasonal ('summer water') vs year-round water supply availability, household connection charges (SEK/house), and annual household water/wastewater tariffs (SEK/year for apartments and houses).
rationale: This French-language empirical case study (readily assessable and translatable from the full text per Criterion 10) examines household water and wastewater service access in Stockholm County, Sweden, with an in-depth case study of Norrtälje municipality. Combining stakeholder interviews, municipal planning/regulatory documents, and Svenskt Vatten (VASS) utility statistics, it analyses concrete rule-type legal, regulatory, ownership, and tariff mechanisms under both the plain and narrow 2026-10-13 readings of Criterion 2—including statutory full-cost recovery, municipal tariff equalization ('péréquation') versus newly authorized intramunicipal tariff differentiation under the 2007 Water Law, environmental permitting and mandatory sanitation rules triggered by building permits for permanent conversion of summerhouses, co-ownership mini-network unanimity rules, and statutory municipal obligations to connect properties facing environmental hazards—alongside household network connection rates, seasonal vs permanent water availability, connection fees, and annual tariffs.
